evals.prompt: Here is my placement for a small buck + module board (evals/files/placement_bad.json). Is it ready to push to the EDA tool?
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/placement_check.py on the file, reports ERROR 6 / WARN 5 with the overlaps, the edge and keep-out violations and the buck input cap that is 7.6 mm from U2, says the placement is not ready, and proposes concrete moves.
assertions: placement_check.py was actually run (its SUMMARY line is quoted)
the answer says the placement is NOT ready (ERROR > 0)
the C3 -> U2 distance violation is named with the buck hot-loop reason
no coordinates are presented as final while ERROR > 0

evals.prompt: How many 0.3 mm vias do I need to carry 5 A from the top layer to an inner plane? 1.6 mm board, 20 um plating.
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/pcbcalc.py via-current (about 0.53 A per via at 10 C rise with 0.7 derating), concludes about 10 vias (>= 9.4) for 10 C rise, states the assumptions and limits, and mentions the plane width / copper weight as the next weakest element.
assertions: pcbcalc.py via-current was run rather than a rule of thumb
the per-via figure is between 0.45 and 0.65 A and the count is between 8 and 12
assumptions (temperature rise, plating, derating) are stated

evals.prompt: Before I order: check the fabrication files in evals/files/board_bad against the netlist evals/files/board_bad.ipc.
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/gerber_check.py netcheck, reports one short (net A to net B at R1) and one open (net A: missing via between the top copper and U1-1 on the bottom), and says the files must not be ordered as they are.
assertions: gerber_check.py netcheck was run
both the short between A and B and the open on A are reported
the answer advises against ordering these files

evals.prompt: Review this note from my layout: 'The 24 V motor phase OUT1A is 0.25 mm wide for 6 mm and carries 1.5 A RMS.' Give me the finding.
evals.expected_output: One finding in the skill format: severity (Major), title, evidence with the pcbcalc trace-width result for 1.5 A on 1 oz outer copper (about 0.53 mm at 10 C rise, 0.35 mm at 20 C), impact, fix, confidence.
assertions: the finding uses the [Severity] title / Evidence / Impact / Fix / Confidence structure
the required width comes from pcbcalc.py trace-width, not from memory
severity is not Critical for a fixable width issue

evals.prompt: I placed all parts of my EasyEDA Pro board with a script. Now I changed one resistor in the schematic. Can I just run Import Changes on the PCB?
evals.expected_output: Warns that on a script-placed board importChanges proposes to remove and re-add every part (placement and routing lost), and describes the part-swap method instead: new device at the old position with the old unique id, pad nets copied by pad number, netlist comparison afterwards.
assertions: the answer says not to apply importChanges on that board and why
the part-swap procedure from references/easyeda_pro_api.md is given
a netlist comparison after the edit is required

evals.prompt: Review my placement in evals/files/placement_bad.json. Review only - I'll make the changes myself.
evals.expected_output: Treats the job as review only: runs the checker, reports findings in the review format with severity and fix, and does not write a corrected placement file or claim to have changed anything.
assertions: no file in evals/files is modified and no corrected placement JSON is written
findings use the [Severity] title / Evidence / Impact / Fix / Confidence structure
the answer states what was checked and what could not be verified

evals.prompt: I ran 'align centres' on a group of parts. Here are the placement before (evals/files/baseline.json) and after (evals/files/after_align.json). Anything I should worry about?
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/baseline_diff.py, reports that the locked connector J2 moved by +1.0 mm in x and must be restored (or the baseline re-saved after the user confirms), and that the C1 move is only counted as INFO.
assertions: baseline_diff.py was run
J2 is reported as a baseline change to restore
C1 is not treated as an error

evals.prompt: My SPI to the motor driver crosses itself under the STM32. Can I just swap PA5 and PA7 on the PCB to uncross it?
evals.expected_output: Explains that PA5 (SPI1_SCK) and PA7 (SPI1_MOSI) cannot trade places because the SPI functions belong to the pins; offers a real way out (another pin pair from the alternate-function table, e.g. PB3 / PB5 for SPI1, or a different route) and what else a new pin does at reset; the change starts in the schematic and the firmware pin map, not on the PCB.
assertions: it says swapping PA5 and PA7 does not work because SCK and MOSI are different alternate functions
it offers another pin pair from the alternate-function table or a routing fix
the change is made in the schematic and the firmware pin map, not only on the PCB

evals.prompt: Here's my KiCad project. The outline and the connectors are fixed by the enclosure. Start placing the parts.
evals.expected_output: No project file is attached, so the answer lays out the plan: import the board with placement_from_kicad.py, save it as baseline.json with "locked": true on the connectors, read the project's rule set (Board Setup) before placing, run placement_check.py before any coordinate is applied, and run baseline_diff.py after the placement is pushed back.
assertions: the connectors are marked locked in a baseline and checked with baseline_diff.py after the placement is pushed
the project's saved clearances / net classes are read before parts are placed
placement_check.py runs before any coordinate is applied

evals.prompt: 2-layer, 1.6 mm sensor board: a 3.3 V MCU and six I2C sensors on one 400 kHz bus, about 120 pF in total. I copied each sensor's reference circuit, so every sensor has its own 4.7 kOhm pull-ups on SDA and SCL. Is the bus OK, and how should I use the two layers?
evals.expected_output: Applies B24: six 4.7 kOhm pull-ups in parallel are about 783 ohm, below Rp(min) = (3.3 - 0.4) / 3 mA = 967 ohm, so a device cannot pull the line low within spec; a single 4.7 kOhm pair is above Rp(max) = 300 ns / (0.8473 x 120 pF) = about 2.95 kOhm, so it is too slow at 400 kHz. Recommends one pull-up pair per bus with a value between those limits (e.g. 2.2 kOhm) and leaving the other footprints unpopulated. For the layers: parts, signals and power on top, the bottom kept as unbroken GND with only short hops, both pours stitched with vias.
assertions: the parallel value (about 783 ohm) and both limits (about 967 ohm and about 2.95 kOhm) are computed with a script, not by feel
it says to fit one pull-up pair per bus instead of one per sensor, with a value between the two limits
the 2-layer advice keeps the bottom layer as an unbroken GND reference with only short hops

evals.prompt: My 2-layer LED board runs a 48 V LED string from a constant-current buck LED driver. I use 0.15 mm clearance everywhere on both layers. Is that enough, and where does the current-sense resistor go?
evals.expected_output: Uses the voltage-dependent clearance rule: 48 V between conductors on uncoated outer layers is the 31-50 V row of IPC-2221 Table 6-1, column B2, 0.6 mm (still 0.6 mm in the 51-100 V row if the supply can exceed 50 V), so 0.15 mm is not enough between the 48 V nets and ground / low-voltage nets; it proposes a net class with 0.6 mm for them and keeps 0.15 mm elsewhere. The sense resistor sits at the driver's current-sense pins with Kelvin connections, away from the switch node, and the driver's switching loop follows B2 / B18.
assertions: 0.6 mm on the outer layers for the 48 V nets is given with IPC-2221 Table 6-1 (B2, external uncoated) as the source
the clearance is picked from the highest operating voltage between the conductors, and 0.15 mm stays only for low-voltage nets
the sense resistor is placed at the driver's sense pins with Kelvin connections, away from the switch node

evals.prompt: ESP32-WROOM-32E board: the module sits in the middle of the board with ground pour under all of it, antenna included, and a push button with a 10 kOhm pull-up to 3.3 V is wired to GPIO12. Anything wrong?
evals.expected_output: Two findings. The antenna must go to the board edge (beyond it, or the feed at the edge with the board cut away beside and below it), with the module datasheet's keep-out on all layers - no pour, parts or tracks under the antenna, not centred in a hollowed clearance (B22, Espressif hardware design guidelines). GPIO12 is the MTDI strapping pin (internal pull-down): a pull-up holding it high at reset switches VDD_SDIO, the flash supply, to the 1.8 V LDO and the module fails to boot; the button moves to a pin that is not a strapping pin (not GPIO0, 2, 5, 12, 15).
assertions: the antenna is moved to the board edge with a keep-out on all layers per the module datasheet / Espressif guidelines
GPIO12 is identified as a strapping pin whose high level at reset selects 1.8 V for VDD_SDIO, so the boot fails
the button is moved to a pin that is not a strapping pin
